title: SLoRA: Scalable Serving of Thousands of LoRA Adapters
problem: Serving thousands of different LoRA adapters concurrently requires prohibitive memory and compute resources, as naive approaches load each adapter independently. Existing systems only scale to dozens of adapters.
motivation: Multi-tenant LLM inference systems need to serve many customized models via parameter-efficient LoRA adapters for different users and tasks simultaneously.
method: SLoRA uses intelligent scheduling and memory virtualization to enable thousands of concurrent adapters on limited GPU resources. The system employs dynamic adapter loading/unloading, request batching across adapters, memory pooling, and prefix caching to reduce per-adapter overhead and maximize resource utilization.
key_novelty: First system to demonstrate serving thousands of LoRA adapters through efficient scheduling and memory virtualization on commodity GPUs.
contributions: Scheduling algorithm for efficient adapter batching and memory placement
Memory virtualization layer for managing thousands of adapters
Demonstration of 1000+ concurrent adapters on single GPU
10-20x throughput improvement over naive per-adapter serving
limitations: Specific hardware constraints and workload limitations not discussed in title.
primary_theme: Scalable multi-tenant LLM inference with parameter-efficient adapters
